title: Three consumed contracts of the pack-recovery step have no dependency row, and the plan gives the two stories no contract or integration dependency
source: Template and Rules v1 §R5.4 dependency classes and §R5.5 DP table rows DP-03, DP-13 and DP-19; the metadata rows of RWB-S4-E5006-APP (Depends on (build) = RWB-S4-E5006-CON, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-N001-CON; Contract, Integration and External dependencies = None) and of RWB-S4-E5006-CON (all four None); the plan slice list of the legacy key; Architecture v5 slide 41 (rwb-document owns metadata, custody, OCR text and fields, signatures, retention) and slide 19 (rwb-litigation IN: REST GET/POST /legal-actions, GET/POST /hearings; EVT NoticeDelivered, PartnerResultSubmitted)
section: Sections 3, 12.2, 12.8, 12.9 and 13 and the fragment keys ops_consumed, C, I of both stories
description: Both stories consume three things that no metadata row carries: the document checklist read and the case document page of rwb-document (P5), and the case-move answer of rwb-case (P3). The ownership of the document is unambiguous in Architecture v5 slide 41 and in the Ownership Map, so the read cannot be turned into a table read without breaking DP-01 and DP-05, and no source gives the case-move answer an operation name. The metadata rows are kept exactly as the plan gives them, with Contract, Integration and External dependencies None, so the three rows are declared in 12.2 as consumed and faked and the build sequence is unchanged. A reader of the metadata alone would conclude that the step needs only its own contract and the two platform contracts.
evidence: Template and Rules v1 R5.5: DP-03 adds H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, DP-19 adds H RWB-PLT-N001-CON, DP-13 adds none; the patterns applied to both stories are DP03, DP13 and DP19 only; the metadata rows of both stories name no contract, integration or external dependency; RWB-P5-E1040-APP publishes GET /cases/{caseId}/document-checklist (API-P5-008) and RWB-P5-E1026-APP publishes GET /cases/{caseId}/documents (API-P5-002), and no P5 contract story carries either as its own baseline; the TSD S4 v2 T-A.1 inventory holds API-S4-001 to API-S4-005 and no document or case operation; no source names a case move operation and the retrieval request is described only in prose
area: Dependency map and build sequencing, S4 rwb-litigation with P5 rwb-document and P3 rwb-case
owner_role: Solution architect, S4 rwb-litigation, with the P5 rwb-document and P3 rwb-case architects
proposed: Carry the three rows as non-blocking consumed contracts in the Dependency Map, name the two document reads after the P5 stories that publish them, and have the rwb-case owner confirm the case-move answer when its contract story is written; leave the metadata rows of the plan unchanged.

title: The recovery element, the gap reason and the list the reason is drawn from have no field list in any source
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md heading RWB-E5-006 (Data table: recovery_case, document, decision_log_entry, rule_row; Endpoints: POST /cases/{caseId}/legal-actions, GET /legal-actions/{legalActionId}); FSD S4 v3 A2.6.3.2 field catalogue (legal_action columns only); TSD S4 v2 T3.1 (legal_action DF-LEG-001 to DF-LEG-014, hearing DF-LEG-024 to DF-LEG-029, no pack or recovery column); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-18 and R-LIT-19 (record the gap with a reason)
section: Sections 3, 7, 11, 12.2, 12.5, 12.8 and 14 of both stories and the fragment keys ops_consumed and C
description: The recovery path needs three things that no source specifies: the element that carries the recovery outcome of an item, the element that carries the reason of an unrecoverable item, and the list the reason is drawn from. The legacy story lists the document and the decision log in its data table and no pack field, the FSD field catalogue lists only legal_action columns, and the TSD lists legal_action and hearing with no column for an item state, an outcome or a reason. R-LIT-19 requires the gap to be recorded with a reason but names no field and no list. Both stories therefore carry the recovery element as an element of the contract with the placeholder, record the outcome and the reason in the decision record, and write no business table column.
evidence: The legacy data table of RWB-E5-006 lists recovery_case, document, decision_log_entry and rule_row only; FSD S4 A2.6.3.2 lists legal_action.case_id, law_firm_id, action_type, lawsuit_no, black_case_no, red_case_no, court_name and claim_amount; TSD S4 T3.1 ends at DF-LEG-014 for legal_action and DF-LEG-029 for hearing; no LOV of recovery reasons appears in the reference data list of the module; Architecture v5 slide 19 gives rwb-litigation only REST GET/POST /legal-actions and GET/POST /hearings
area: Contract shape and physical model, S4 rwb-litigation with P5 rwb-document
owner_role: Tech lead, S4 rwb-litigation, with the P5 rwb-document analyst and the business analyst of EP05
proposed: Add the recovery element to the API specification of the service and, if the gap reason must be a stored fact, add it to the LDM and to the DB story of the service with a reason list owned by the business; rewrite the placeholder rows of the two stories when it exists.

title: The legacy master carries no requirement identifier for RWB-E5-006, so both stories trace to the feature and to the nearest module requirement
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md heading RWB-E5-006 (metadata table: Epic, Module, Feature FEAT-LIT-06, Process, Priority, Depends on FEAT-LIT-05, Decision); _work/msr/plan/legacy_index.json entry RWB-E5-006 with reqs = []; FSD S4 v3 requirements served (REQ-S4-002) and A2.6; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 row FEAT-LIT-06
section: Sections 2 and 18 of both stories and the reqs key of both fragments
description: The legacy story RWB-E5-006 carries no REQ identifier: its metadata table names the feature FEAT-LIT-06 and the prerequisite FEAT-LIT-05 and no requirement row, and the plan's legacy index records an empty requirement list. The FSD S4 requirements table holds REQ-S4-002, 'a litigation pack is assembled and checked against the document checklist, and missing documents are requested', which is the requirement the feature serves, but the mapping is made here and not by the source. Both stories trace to FEAT-LIT-06, to REQ-S4-002 and to the L3 process 08 Litigate and enforce. Nothing blocks the build; the exposure is a traceability report whose requirement link rests on a mapping the PRD of EP05 has not confirmed.
evidence: The metadata table of RWB-E5-006 has seven rows and no requirement row; the legacy index of the run records reqs: [] for the key; FSD S4 v3 requirements served lists REQ-S4-002 with the text on the pack checklist and missing documents; the Epics 3 to 8 specification row for FEAT-LIT-06 gives Epic E5, Module S4, Kind User, Primary role Litigation officer, Systems the Workbench document hub and CCMS, Depends on FEAT-LIT-05 and no requirement
area: Traceability and requirements, EP05, S4 rwb-litigation
owner_role: Business analyst, S4 rwb-litigation, with the PRD owner of EP05
proposed: Confirm REQ-S4-002 as the requirement of the feature in the Epics 3 to 8 PRD, or add a dedicated requirement for the recovery of a missing document, and rewrite the requirement column of both stories and of their fragments when it is confirmed.

title: The catalogue gives the litigation topic three events and none of them is the recovery of a pack item, so the step publishes and consumes nothing
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 19 (rwb-litigation OUT: EVT rwb.litigation.events.v1: LawsuitFiled, JudgmentRecorded, AuctionResult; IN: EVT NoticeDelivered, PartnerResultSubmitted) and slide 43 (row: JudgmentRecorded, AuctionResult with producers rwb-litigation and consumers rwb-asset and rwb-case); Event and Messaging Design v4 EV-16 DocumentStored and EV-17 DocumentFieldsExtracted, published by the document hub; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-09 and the pattern set of this key
section: Sections 2, 12.3, 12.4 and 19 of both stories and the events_published and events_consumed keys of both fragments
description: A recovered, re-created or unrecoverable pack item is a fact that another service may want — the document hub itself, the case or reporting — but the event catalogue of Architecture v5 gives rwb-litigation three events that belong to the filing, the judgment and the auction result, and the only document events of the legacy catalogue are DocumentStored and DocumentFieldsExtracted, published by the document hub. DP-09 is not in either story's pattern set, no outbox row or producer is added, and no source states that the recovery outcome is an event. Declaring one would put an event into the build that no owner assigned, and omitting it silently would leave the outcome visible only on the P5 and P3 answers. Both stories therefore publish nothing and the assignment is recorded here.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 19 'EVT rwb.litigation.events.v1: LawsuitFiled, JudgmentRecorded, AuctionResult' and 'EVT NoticeDelivered, PartnerResultSubmitted' on the IN side; slide 43 lists JudgmentRecorded and AuctionResult with their consumers and gives LawsuitFiled no consumer row; Event and Messaging Design v4 EV-16 and EV-17 name the document hub as the publisher of the two document events; the patterns applied to both stories are DP03, DP13 and DP19 and none is DP-09
area: Event contract, S4 rwb-litigation with P5 rwb-document and P3 rwb-case
owner_role: Solution architect, S4 rwb-litigation, with the event platform owner and the P5 and P3 analysts
proposed: Decide once, in the event catalogue of the service, whether a recovery outcome raises an event and who publishes it: if P5 owns the item state, keep the outcome on the P5 contract and publish nothing here; if a litigation event is wanted, add it to the catalogue, add DP-09 and the outbox row to RWB-S4-E5006-APP and name its consumers.

title: The FSD integration point CCMS has no owner in the target and no external dependency row
source: FSD S4 v3 A2.6.2 integration points ('the Workbench document hub, CCMS'); Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 row FEAT-LIT-06 (systems: the Workbench document hub, CCMS); Architecture v5 slide 41 (P2 rwb-integration owns interface config, file runs, outbound items and ACE integration paths) and slide 8 (outside systems); the External dependencies row of both stories (None)
description: The feature names two integration points, the Workbench document hub and CCMS. The hub is rwb-document (P5) and is declared in 12.2. CCMS is an external case-management system of the courts or the bank, named nowhere else in the target: Architecture v5 does not list it among the outside systems of slide 8, the interface inventory does not give it an INT identifier of its own for this feature, and no story owns the path. Whether the item request of the recovery path reaches CCMS directly, through rwb-document or through rwb-integration (P2) is therefore undecided, and neither story declares an external dependency. The recovery path is specified against the P5 contract only, and the CCMS leg is out of scope until its owner is named.
evidence: FSD S4 A2.6.2 'Integration points. the Workbench document hub, CCMS'; the Epics 3 to 8 specification repeats 'the Workbench document hub, CCMS' for FEAT-LIT-06; Architecture v5 slide 8 lists partners, Entra ID, the notification path, the WIN file, the debt-buyer files, Enterprise AI and the data lake as the outside systems and not CCMS; slide 41 gives rwb-integration the interface config, the file runs, the outbound items and the ACE integration paths; the External dependencies row of both stories is None
area: Integration and external systems, EP05, S4 rwb-litigation with P5 rwb-document and P2 rwb-integration
owner_role: Solution architect, with the P2 rwb-integration and P5 rwb-document architects and the interface owner of CCMS
proposed: Name the owner of the CCMS leg once: if the document hub fronts CCMS, keep the P5 contract as the only path and record it in the P5 interface specification; if rwb-integration fronts it, add the interface row and an X dependency to the operations story of the legacy key rather than to the app story.
